content:
anya: Quick prioritization thread for next sprint: we have 12 catalog onboards queued, 3 customer-driven urgent asks, and engineering capacity limited. Need a clear rubric to pick top 4.

fred: Can we prioritize by expected ARR impact + churn risk? I have rough numbers for the 3 urgent customers.

marie: Also factor technical risk: models that require compat shims (embeds/mismatched schemas) will need additional work and possibly legal approval.

tom: Ops note: onboarding that needs dedicated pools will delay other jobs; estimate 2x infra lead time. We should avoid unexpected pool reservations mid-sprint.

sam: Proposal for prioritization rubric: 
1) Customer urgency (paid + churn window) 40%
2) Revenue/ARR impact 30%
3) Engineering effort (low->high) -20%
4) Compliance/regulatory blockers -10% (deduct)
This scores and ranks the queue.

anya: Good start. We need hard thresholds to pick exactly 4. Suggested cutoffs: score >= 60 -> sprint slot; 45-59 -> backlog grooming; <45 -> defer.

fred: For the 3 urgent: Cust A (enterprise fintech) score 78 (wants 30d pin), Cust B (start-up) 64, Cust C (marketing) 52. That gives two immediate slots.

marie: Engineering caveat: Cust A requires an embed-schema exception and legal addendum. Need legal sign-off before we commit to pin. Legal-bot, can we get turnaround in 48h?

legal-bot: Legal intake: request logged RA-2026-17. Standard review SLA 3 business days; expedited review possible with PO/CS justification.

sam: For the remaining slots, we should pick low-effort high-impact models. From the backlog, model X (open LLM) is low effort and high ARR upside -> score 66. Model Y requires quantization tuning -> score 52.

anya: That gives final four: Cust A, Cust B, model X, and Cust C (pending legal). But we need a fallback if legal delays. Option: reserve a soft slot for model Z (quick) if Cust C blocks.

tom: Agree. Also callout: ensure bench lanes - if any fastlane requests granted we follow the mini-canary pattern and reserve a pre-warmed pool. That must be planned in sprint planning.

bench-bot: queued bench runs required for selected onboards: mini_canary (500 samples) for Cust A and Cust B; full bench for model X.

marie: Action items: 
- sam: produce score sheet + raw inputs (due EOD)
- legal-bot: flag RA-2026-17 for expedited review (ask: CS to attach justification)
- tom: block pool capacity for 48h windows and publish cost delta (due before sprint planning)
- anya: update roadmap board and notify sales/CS of slots (due tomorrow)

anya: Decision: tentatively approve those 4 with contingency: if legal not signed for Cust A by sprint start we replace with model Z. We'll communicate expectations to sales.

fred: I'll get CS to add PO and justification for legal.

sam: I'll post the scoring spreadsheet and bench job configs.

anya: Thanks. Let's keep this lightweight and repeatable; we should bake this rubric into the catalog intake form for future sprints.

marie: Agreed. Also propose a small doc outlining exceptions (embed pins, compliance, adapter paths) so PMs can estimate hit quickly.

anya: OK closing thread. We'll review final roster at sprint planning tomorrow 10:00.

bench-bot: scheduled jobs created: bb-1798812345-1 (custA mini_canary), bb-1798812345-2 (custB mini_canary), bb-1798812345-3 (modelX full_bench).
